brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 girls' birthday evites (unicorns, princess castles, mermaids, fairy gardens, butterflies, ballet, cupcakes, rainbows, kittens, art studio, carousel, pop star), several with scratch-and-reveal. Push past the pink-and-glitter default without losing what kids actually love.
brief.audience: Parents of 3 to 10 year olds; the kids are the first viewers.
brief.feeling: Enchantment with real craft; delight that feels hand-made.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
references: Exploration grid A: pastel 3D baby unicorns on cotton-candy clouds with balloons, a crescent-moon nap, a rainbow; very sweet, very pink.
Exploration grid B: luminous underwater kingdoms, coral, jellyfish, an open shell with pearls, god-rays through turquoise water; no characters.

proposals.title: The Illuminated Page, Reborn
proposals.idea: Each evite is structured as a medieval illuminated manuscript folio — a strict ruled measure governs every element, the art plate lives within a gilded architectural border, and the scratch-and-reveal uncovers a hidden devotional image the way a vellum flap once concealed a saint — so that enchantment arrives through proportion and concealment, not through saturation and scatter.
proposals.geometry: A fixed 390×690px canvas divided on a 12-column, 18-row modular grid with a 24px baseline. The outer border is a procedurally generated architectural frame — pointed arches for princess castles, coral tracery for mermaids, interlaced vine for fairy gardens — occupying exactly 3 columns on each side and 2 rows top and bottom, leaving a centered 252×552px illuminated field. The scratch zone occupies the lower third of that field, a strict horizontal band whose reveal boundary is a clean arch, not a ragged scribble. Text sits in the bottom 4 rows below the frame, never inside the art plate. The QR code occupies the lower-right corner cell of the border itself, disguised as a heraldic roundel.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cinzel (Google Fonts, OFL) — Roman capitals, tracked at +80, set at 28px for the child's name field, 18px for date and venue. Secondary body: IM Fell English (Google Fonts, OFL) — italic, 13px, loose leading at 1.8, used for the invitation text block. No third face. Drop caps on the first line of body text, sized to 3 baseline units, rendered in the same foil shader as the border. Case is mixed: display caps, body sentence case. No script typeface — the Fell italic already carries warmth without sentimentality.
proposals.imageLogic: All art plates are Magnific generative outputs directed by theme-specific prompts (see productionMethod). The plate is never a full-bleed photograph; it is a painted panel inside the architectural frame — the frame occludes its edges as a triptych panel occludes its ground. The foreground cut-outs (drifting on phone tilt) are isolated generative elements — a single unicorn, a single butterfly, a crown — rendered with physically-plausible subsurface scattering so they read as illuminated vellum figures, not PNG stickers. No photographic source enters the pipeline; every image is generative or procedural.
proposals.texture: The art plate carries a vellum grain shader: high-frequency noise at 0.4 opacity simulating stretched calfskin tooth, warm cream undertone (#F5ECD7), directional fiber lines at 7-degree tilt. The architectural border uses a thin gold foil shader — not glitter, not confetti, but burnished leaf: specular highlight locked to a single top-left motivated light source (enforcing the unified light grammar I have been developing; this is a structural act, not decoration). The background behind the frame is a deep ink wash — prussian blue for mermaid, forest shadow for fairy garden, midnight for pop star — so the illuminated field reads as a lit window in a dark room.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the architectural border draws itself along its own linework at 600ms, cubic-ease-in-out, as if a ruling pen is traveling the frame — this is a single CSS path animation, lightweight, no JavaScript required. At rest: the art plate breathes with a 0.3px vertical drift at 4s period, simulating the slight curl of real vellum. On phone tilt: foreground cut-outs parallax at ±8px with a 120ms spring decay (strict, governed, not loose — the escapement principle I noted). Scratch-and-reveal: the reveal mask is a WebGL fragment shader; as the user's finger crosses the band, the hidden devotional image emerges with a foil shimmer that blooms from the touch point outward, fading to the unified light source within 400ms. Particle system: theme-specific — gold motes for princess, bioluminescent drift for mermaid, pollen float for fairy garden — maximum 40 particles, opacity-keyed, never obs
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids. Grid 1 (12 plates, one per theme): 'illuminated manuscript panel, [theme adjective] subject, gouache and gold leaf on vellum, medieval folio painting, warm cream ground, single top-left light source, no text, no border, centered composition, 4:7 ratio, ultra-detailed, OFL art, original characters, no copyrighted IP' — returns 8–16 variants per theme; editorial selection picks the single strongest plate per theme. Grid 2 (foreground cut-outs, all 12 themes in one prompt): 'isolated [theme character or object], illuminated manuscript figure style, subsurface scattering, vellum ground, transparent background, single top-left light, no shadow on ground plane' — returns isolated elements for the drift layer. Architectural border: procedurally generated per theme in GLSL — a parametric arch-and-tracery shader that accepts a theme token (UNICORN, MERMAID, etc.) and ou
proposals.humanTrace: The vellum grain shader is calibrated against the directional fiber of real calfskin — the angle (7 degrees) and frequency are derived from archival manuscript photography in the public domain (British Library digitized collection, pre-1500, no rights restriction). The ruling-pen border animation follows the actual sequence a scribe would rule — horizontal rails first, then verticals, then arch curves — so the drawing order is editorially motivated, not random. The foil highlight vector is fixed to the same top-left source across every layer and every theme, so the light is consistent the way a single candle in a scriptorium is consistent. These choices are perceptible: a viewer who has held an illuminated book will feel the grammar.
proposals.risk: The risk is that parents read 'medieval manuscript' and think 'school project' before they think 'enchantment.' The counter is that children do not read genre; they read luminosity, concealment, and the promise of something hidden — and the illuminated format delivers all three with more structural authority than a glitter scatter ever could. The second risk is load time: the GLSL border shader must be fallback-safe; a static SVG border must render if WebGL is unavailable, and I am confident that is engineerable within the Tela constraint.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a fanfare of particles, a dramatic light bloom, a swell of motion that declares the moment. I insist the reveal should be quiet and consequential: the foil shimmer blooms from touch and then resolves to stillness, because a reveal that keeps performing after it has landed is an actor who will not leave the stage. proposals.title: Ink-Stamped Wonder, Not Glitter-Poured
proposals.idea: Each evite is a hand-press print that a child could have made — linocut-style marks, ink bleed, registration drift — given a single committed light source and a foil varnish that clings only to the carved edges, so the screen proves the block existed first.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile crop. Composition built on an off-center vertical spine — not a centered mandala, not a grid — so the main image sits at roughly the upper two-thirds like a broadside poster torn from a wall. Text block drops into the lower third on a raw ink-washed ground, left-aligned, ragged right. Foreground cut-outs (drifting petals, stars, fins, butterflies) occupy the negative corner space, never the center. The twelve plates share this spine but each breaks it differently: unicorn bleeds left, mermaid bleeds right, pop star crowds the top edge.
proposals.typography: Headings: Fraunces (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable optical size, high contrast, slightly swollen serifs that read as hand-set letterpress at display sizes. Body/details: DM Mono for date/time/venue — it reads like a rubber-stamp address block. NO script faces. Case: sentence case only, never all-caps glitter-font shouting. Tracking: tight on the headline (-0.02em), loose on the mono detail line (+0.08em). Size contrast is violent: headline at 52px, detail at 13px, nothing in between.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates directed as linocut-style illustrations with visible gouge marks, ink spread at block edges, and deliberate misregistration of a second color layer (a warm yellow or deep teal ghost shifted 4–6px). The plates are NOT photographic. They read as printed matter. Prompt direction for the one master Magnific grid: 'twelve square-format linocut illustration plates, children's birthday themes — unicorn, princess castle, mermaid, fairy garden, butterfly, ballet, cupcake, rainbow, kitten, art studio, carousel, pop star — each rendered as a two-color relief print, visible gouge texture, ink bleed at edges, misregistered second color in warm gold offset 5px upper-left, white paper tooth showing through, no photography, no gradients, flat ink fields only, high contrast, age 4–10 wonder without pink-glitter default, each plate compositionally distinct.' Second Magnific pass
proposals.texture: Paper tooth is the base: a procedural shader (WebGL, already in Tela's effects layer) lays down a cream-white ground with visible fiber grain — not a texture overlay slapped on top, but the actual background color rendered through a grain displacement map so the ink fields look absorbed, not printed on glass. The foil shimmer (Tela WebGL) is restricted to the carved-edge zones of each linocut mark — it does not flood the image, it traces the ridge. This is my rule: digital sheen earned only where the physical dent would be. Ink bleed zones get a subtle wet-spread bokeh that is NOT decorative — it marks where ink was heaviest.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the plate drops in with a 0.3s stamp-impact — slight vertical compression then release, as if a press arm came down. This is the only entrance animation. Foreground cut-outs (petals, fins, stars) drift on gyroscope tilt at 0.04 parallax multiplier, slow, 60fps, eased. They do NOT bounce or pulse on loop — they respond only to the phone moving. Scratch-and-reveal (unicorn, mermaid, pop star, rainbow): the reveal layer is a WebGL mask that responds to touch drag; underneath is a second ink-color plate (the misregistered ghost becomes the prize image) — the scratch texture is generated as a dry-ink scrape, not a digital sparkle wipe. Foil shimmer on carved edges animates at 2s loop, subtle, motion-path follows the gouge direction, stops if reduced-motion is on. Candle flicker (cupcake plate): single warm point light, physically plausible, 1.2s irregular loop, reduced-motion replac
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid (8–16 plates, flat cost) returns all twelve base illustrations. Editorial selection picks the twelve strongest compositional reads. Two plates get a second-pass refinement prompt. Plates import into Tela as the locked art layer. Foreground cut-outs are generated as separate Magnific passes with transparent-compatible prompts ('isolated on white, clean edge') then masked in Tela. WebGL paper-grain shader and foil-edge shader are written in GLSL and stored as Tela effect presets reusable across the collection. All twelve share the same shader stack — only the foil color and grain density change per theme. Live text (Fraunces + DM Mono) sits above all layers in Tela's text engine, never baked. Load budget: art plates exported at WebP, max 280kb each; shaders are <8kb; foreground cut-outs are SVG where possible, WebP otherwise.
proposals.humanTrace: The gouge marks in the linocut plates are the trace — they are directed to be visible, directional, and inconsistent (the prompt specifies 'visible gouge texture, not uniform'). The misregistration is a directed decision about where the ghost color lands. The stamp-impact entrance is timed to 0.3s because that is how long a press arm takes — that number came from a decision, not a default. The foil traces the carved edge because someone (me, in the prompt direction) decided the light source is upper-left, consistent across all twelve plates, so the shimmer is always a record of that one committed sun.
proposals.risk: Kids and parents expect shimmer-as-decoration. This gives them shimmer-as-evidence. Some parents will read 'linocut' as craft-class cheap and not premium. The risk is worth it because the alternative — more pastel 3D renders with confetti particles — is what every other birthday evite platform already does, and Plajah's only differentiation is craft that feels real. The stamp-impact entrance risks feeling abrupt; it is abrupt on purpose, because a press arm does not ease in.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will layer gold, volumetric light, and cascading foreground elements until the linocut grain is buried under atmosphere. I expect them to argue that children need drama and that restraining the foil to carved edges is withholding. I disagree: the drama here is in the contrast between flat ink fields and the single glinting edge — flood the foil and you lose the contrast, whic

proposals.title: Simulation Knows the Rules
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physically-simulated diorama — a coherent light source, a defined depth stack, and a single interaction rule — so that every shimmer, tilt response, and particle follows one spatial logic rather than stacking unrelated effects.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 viewport. Three explicit depth planes: background plate (fixed), mid-ground cut-outs (parallax at 0.4× tilt gain), foreground micro-elements (parallax at 1.0× tilt gain). All twelve designs share this plane contract. Compositional anchor is always a center-weighted primary subject occupying 55–65% of vertical height, with negative breathing room at top and bottom to hold live text without cropping. Scratch-and-reveal panels are rectangular masks inset 16px from edge, corners at 12px radius, sized to cover exactly 40% of the plate — never arbitrary — so the hidden content is always a full compositional layer, not a decorative patch.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Fraunces (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable optical size axis cranked to 144pt, italic, soft-serif; reads as hand-lettered at distance but is geometrically anchored. Secondary / date-venue: DM Sans Light, 13–15px, tracked +20, sentence case. No script faces; Fraunces's optical-size variation does the warmth work without the legibility cost of a cursive. Text always lives above the WebGL layer so foil shimmer does not bleed onto letterforms — the shimmer is the frame, not the word.
proposals.imageLogic: All plates are Magnific generative outputs directed as physically-based renders: single motivated light source declared per design (e.g., Unicorn = upper-left 40° diffuse daylight through cloud; Mermaid = caustic god-ray from upper-right 25°; Ballet = raked stage-left theatrical key). That declared source angle is the constraint that propagates: the foil highlight direction in the WebGL layer matches it, parallax shadow offsets match it, bokeh bloom origin matches it. No plate is accepted from the draft grid unless its internal shadows are consistent with the declared source. Foreground cut-outs are separately generated on transparent fields and composited in Tela — they are not masked from the plate, so their lighting is independent and can be tuned. No photographic stock.
proposals.texture: Simulated physical surfaces, not applied filters. Unicorn / Princess / Fairy / Butterfly / Ballet / Carousel: parchment-weight paper tooth (Magnific: 'cold-press watercolor paper under raking light, 400dpi, visible fiber') as the ground of the plate — not a texture overlay but baked into the generation prompt so shadows fall into the grain. Mermaid / Rainbow: simulated wet glass or resin surface — caustic refraction patterns generated as a WebGL normal-map layer. Cupcakes / Art Studio / Pop Star / Kittens: matte gouache finish, brushstroke edge visible at subject boundary, generated as part of the plate not as a post-process stroke. Foil shimmer (WebGL): single-channel specular mask, painted procedurally along the declared light angle — it moves with gyroscope input at 6° lag so it feels physically attached to the surface, not floating above it.
proposals.motion: Sequence is a state machine, not an animation timeline. State 0 (load): plate fades in at 280ms, no motion. State 1 (idle): foreground elements drift on gyroscope/DeviceOrientation at 0.4–1.0× gain depending on plane; bokeh particles float upward at 0.3px/frame, looped with a 4-frame random offset per particle so they do not march in sync; foil shimmer updates at 60fps following gyro. State 2 (scratch interaction): pointer/touch drag erases the reveal mask at 40px brush radius; WebGL underneath is a separately composited layer — not a color change but a depth reveal, so the scratched area shows a lower depth plane with its own lighting. State 3 (post-reveal): confetti particles emit from the revealed boundary at 0.8s, physics-based (gravity 0.2, drag 0.05), fade out by 2.4s. Reduced-motion: State 1 collapses to zero parallax and zero particle movement; foil shimmer updates only on explic
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids. Grid 1 (8 plates): Unicorn, Princess Castle, Mermaid, Fairy Garden, Butterfly, Ballet — each with explicit lighting brief embedded in prompt ('single motivated light source upper-left 40°, cold-press paper tooth ground, no characters, original creature design, no Disney reference, 9:19 portrait, painterly but physically grounded'). Grid 2 (8 plates): Cupcakes, Rainbows, Kittens, Art Studio, Carousel, Pop Star — same constraint frame, gouache-finish ground. Foreground cut-outs generated as separate Magnific passes on 100% alpha backgrounds. WebGL layer: GLSL shader written procedurally — specular highlight, bokeh, particle system, scratch mask — no third-party effect library. Tela composites all layers; live text fields are Tela-native. Scratch-and-reveal masks are Tela interaction components, not baked. Total: 2 Magnific grid runs + 1 shader build + Tela assemb
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection from the draft grid is the primary human act: the art director reads each plate's internal shadow logic against the declared light source and rejects any plate where the lighting is inconsistent — that rejection is the craft judgment. Second trace: the specular mask for foil shimmer is hand-drawn in a vector editor as a single stroke following the light angle, then converted to a WebGL texture — the stroke's pressure variation is preserved as mask opacity variation, so the shimmer has a hand-drawn silhouette even though it is rendered computationally. Third trace: particle emitter timing is set by ear against a reference tempo (the rhythm of a child blowing out candles, approximately 1.2s held breath → exhale) — the confetti burst is timed to that biological rhythm, not to a default easing curve.
proposals.risk: The system-logic constraint — one motivated light source per design that must propagate through foil, parallax shadow, and bokeh origin — will reject plates from the Magnific grid that are visually appealing but physically incoherent. That means a higher cull rate and potentially a third grid run. The risk is worth it because the alternative is twelve designs that each feel like a different app opened inside the same frame, which is exactly what the brief is trying to escape. Coherent physics is what separates a diorama from a mood board.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the scratch-and-reveal to be a theatrical event — crescendo shimmer, held suspense, a big burst. I will fight that because a reveal without a spatial rule is a screensaver moment: it impresses once and feels cheap on second open. My reveal is a depth-plane transition governed by the same light source as the rest of the design — the scratched area does not glow diffe

proposals.title: Field Notes from Enchanted Latitudes
proposals.idea: Each invitation is a hand-annotated collector's field plate — the visual language of 19th-century naturalist lithographs and cartographer's marginalia, redrawn entirely in generative imagery and made luminous through WebGL foil that follows the engraved line-work, so the magic reads as discovered, not manufactured.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone canvas. Primary image occupies the top 58%, structured as a botanical/zoological specimen plate with a ruled border (1.5px, ink-simulated, slightly bowed as if printed on damp paper). Marginalia annotations radiate from the central subject at 15–25° angles, set in small caps with leader-dot rules. Bottom 42% is a cream field-note block where live Tela text (name, date, venue) sits in ruled lines — pre-ruled lines are baked into the art plate, live text lands on them. QR and link-preview crop to the top plate only. Foreground cutout layer floats 2–4 specimen fragments (a single wing, a petal, a pearl, a tutu ribbon) that tilt-drift at ±6° parallax. Scratch-and-reveal designs use the field-plate border as the scratch mask: guests scratch the ruled border away to expose the subject beneath a stippled hatch overlay.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — italic for the invitation's 'common name' headline, small-caps for Latin-style specimen labels. Secondary annotation: EB Garamond Regular 11–13px for margin notes and leader lines. Date/venue live text: Cormorant Garamond Regular on the ruled baseline, never baked. All setting is left-aligned or centred on axis; no stacked all-caps shouting. Reduced-motion fallback: type is fully legible static; no text is embedded in the art plate.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generation prompt family: 'naturalist lithograph specimen plate, [subject], fine engraved linework, stippled shading, cream hot-press paper texture, hand-painted watercolour wash over etching, marginalia in iron-gall ink, no modern typography, no photographic elements, isolated on off-white, slight foxing at corners, mid-19th century scientific illustration aesthetic.' One Magnific draft grid of 16 plates covers all 12 themes plus alternates. Each plate is generated at 2048×2048, cropped to subject, then composited in Tela. Foreground cutouts are isolated specimen fragments from the same generation pass, masked to transparency. No photographs. No scans. No third-party illustration. The engraved-line aesthetic is entirely generative but references a documented, non-proprietary visual tradition (European natural history print, pre-copyright).
proposals.texture: Simulated hot-press watercolour paper: procedural shader generating 8–12µm tooth variation, slight cockling at edges. Iron-gall ink bleed on annotation lines: 0.3px feather with warm-brown tint. Stipple dot-field over scratch zones rendered as a WebGL particle mask — dots are NOT uniform; they inherit density from the generated plate's own value map, so the hatch feels drawn, not screened. Foil shimmer (WebGL) is gated strictly to the engraved linework paths extracted from the plate — it does not bleed into the paper ground. This is my standing rule from the block-print work: digital luster must follow physical tool-marks, not float free of them.
proposals.motion: Open sequence (1.8s): plate fades up from cream ground as if a cover sheet is lifted — opacity 0→1 with a simultaneous paper-tooth reveal shader expanding from centre. Foil shimmer activates on engraved lines only, pulsing at 0.4Hz in a slow travelling wave (left→right, mimicking raking light across a cabinet display). Tilt parallax: foreground specimen fragments drift at ±6° lagging 120ms behind device orientation — slow, gravitational, not bouncy. Scratch-and-reveal: finger gesture erases stipple dot layer via WebGL clip path; beneath it, the subject plate is already rendered and waiting — no load on reveal. Candle/bokeh particle layer (birthday themes): 6–10 soft warm bokeh orbs drift upward at 18px/s, opacity 0.3, never obscuring text. Reduced-motion: all animation OFF; foil shimmer reduced to a single static highlight pass baked into the plate composite.
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Write one Magnific prompt family (naturalist plate aesthetic, 12 subject variants) and run a single 16-plate draft grid — one flat cost covers the whole collection plus alternates. 2. Tela compositor receives each plate as a base layer; foreground cutout fragments are isolated from the same generation pass using Tela's generative mask tool. 3. Procedural paper-tooth and ink-bleed shaders are written once and applied as a shared Tela effect preset across all 12 designs — maintenance is a single shader file. 4. WebGL foil mask is generated by extracting luminance edges from the plate (Sobel filter in shader), then thresholding to linework — this is fully automated per plate, no manual masking. 5. Live text rails (ruled lines) are baked into the plate at generation time as a compositional element; Tela text layer snaps to them. 6. Scratch-and-reveal stipple mask is a procedural WebGL lay
proposals.humanTrace: The engraved linework and stipple shading in the generated plates carry the visible pressure logic of a burin or etching needle — directional hatching, swelling strokes, plate-edge bowing. The foil shimmer is constrained to follow those marks exactly, so the digital luster reads as light catching a physical surface that was made by a tool moving through resistance. The paper cockling and foxing are not decorative noise; they are procedurally coherent with the plate's own edge geometry. A child sees sparkle on a drawing; an adult sees a cabinet of wonders. Both are correct.
proposals.risk: The naturalist-plate register skews literary and adult at first glance — a parent previewing the link might hesitate before a child sees it. The risk is worth taking because the subject matter (unicorn, mermaid, kitten) immediately anchors it in childhood delight, and the foil shimmer on the linework is the bridge: it signals magic without signalling cheap. The deeper risk is generative fidelity to the engraved aesthetic — Magnific can drift toward decorative pastiche. Mitigation: tight prompt discipline, reference to specific non-copyrighted plate traditions (Audubon, Gould, Haeckel — all pre-1900, public domain visual vocabulary, no living community's motifs, no sacred imagery, no attribution owed beyond the tradition itself).

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will reach for gilded excess — full-bleed gold grounds, heavy ornamental frames, maximum particle density — and call it wonder. I will stop that direction cold: the foil in this collection is earned by the linework it follows; spread it across the ground and it becomes wallpaper, not magic. Grandeur borrowed from the engraving tradition without the discipline of the engraving traditi

proposals.title: Twelve Miniature Opera Houses
proposals.idea: Each evite is a baroque stage set — a proscenium of layered depth with a single breathtaking reveal moment timed like a curtain rising, where chiaroscuro light, tactile surface simulation, and foreground drift conspire to make a phone screen feel like a jewel box theatre.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 stage framing with a hard architectural arch cut from the top 18% of the plate — the proscenium — below which three to five depth planes recede in forced perspective; the foreground plane bleeds off all four edges creating a sense of being inside the scene rather than looking at a card; scratch-and-reveal panels are inset as trompe-l'oeil curtains, velvet or foil-leafed, occupying the centre 60% width and triggered by swipe rather than tap, so the gesture mirrors the physical act of parting drapes; all twelve share this stage grammar but differ violently in material character: unicorn is spun-sugar rococo, mermaid is Venetian grotto, ballet is gaslit 19th-century wing-and-drop, carousel is Viennese mechanical theatre, pop star is a brutalist concert rig draped in excess.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) at display scale — 52px headline, tracked wide at +120, all caps for the theme word only, set in the proscenium arch zone so it reads before the scene below loads; supporting text in Jost (OFL) Regular 15px, generous leading 1.6, never baked; the contrast between Cormorant's calligraphic stress and Jost's geometric neutrality creates the same tension as a handwritten libretto against a printed playbill; no script faces — the drama is in scale and weight contrast, not in cursive sweetness.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs; all plates are Magnific-directed generative renders described below; image logic is painterly and physically-lit: every plate is directed to simulate a specific light source with a position — a single high-side key imitating a theatrical fresnel, warm 2900K, casting long shadows toward the viewer; secondary fill is cool 6500K bounce from below the frame, simulating stage footlights; this two-source chiaroscuro is non-negotiable across all twelve; plates are rendered at 2× the display size then composited in Tela at 50% scale so the detail reads as richness without loading cost; the mermaid and fairy garden plates reference Bernini's Neptune grotto lighting — deep shadow with a single god-ray; unicorn and cupcake plates reference the confectionary still-life tradition of Jan Davidsz. de Heem — objects lit from upper left against a warm dark ground.
proposals.texture: Simulated materials vary by theme but every plate carries two universal texture passes: a fine paper tooth (220gsm watercolour cold-press simulation, grain at 4% opacity) that makes the digital surface feel pressed rather than printed, and a micro-relief shadow pass that gives foreground cut-outs a 1.5mm raised edge as if die-cut from thick board; theme-specific textures — unicorn: spun sugar and iridescent organza; mermaid: hammered Venetian glass mosaic and wet stone; princess castle: gilded gesso over linen; ballet: worn rosin-dusted sprung floor and silk tulle; carousel: aged lacquer, brass patina, cracked enamel; pop star: brushed aluminium rigging and gel-light haze; all simulated via Magnific material prompts and WebGL normal-map overlays.
proposals.motion: The curtain is the drama; everything else serves it. Sequence: 1. Plate fades up over 0.4s — not a dissolve, a slow reveal from bottom to top like a scrim lifting, driven by a CSS clip-path animation; 2. Foreground cut-outs drift on gyroscope tilt at parallax depth 0.3 — slow, weighted, as if suspended on invisible wires; 3. WebGL foil shimmer pulses once at 1.2s on the proscenium arch trim, then settles to a 4s idle loop at very low amplitude; 4. Scratch-and-reveal: on swipe across the curtain panel a fragment shader dissolves the velvet texture tile by tile in a physically-plausible cloth-wipe direction — left-to-right, slight diagonal, matching the gesture; behind the curtain a secondary scene plate is pre-loaded and fully lit, so the reveal is instantaneous and jaw-dropping; 5. proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids: Grid A directs all twelve plate compositions in a single 16-image batch — prompt structure is 'baroque stage set, [theme], single fresnel key light upper left, cool footlight fill, deep chiaroscuro, [theme-specific material], no characters, no text, 2:1 depth planes, painterly render, 8K detail'; Grid B directs all twelve curtain-behind reveal plates — same lighting grammar, scene advanced: the moment after the curtain parts, the birthday surprise fully lit; Tela compositor receives plates, applies paper-tooth and micro-relief texture passes as WebGL overlays using owned shaders; foreground cut-outs are isolated from plate via generative inpainting then placed on transparent Tela layers; live text zones are masked in the proscenium arch and footer band; foil shimmer is a Plajah-owned WebGL shader applied to the arch trim region via luminance mask.
proposals.humanTrace: The light source position is a creative decision made per plate, not a default — the 2900K fresnel is placed differently for each of the twelve to match the emotional weight of the theme: for mermaid it enters from below and behind, for ballet it rakes from stage-left at 15 degrees, for pop star it is a hard backlight with coloured spill; this positioning is written into each Magnific prompt as a specific vector and is the director's hand inside the machine; additionally the scratch-reveal gesture direction (left-to-right diagonal) is a choreographic decision that makes the child's own swipe the curtain rope — the human trace is the designed performance of the viewer's body.
proposals.risk: Cormorant Garamond at this scale reads sophisticated and slightly adult — parents will love it, but a seven-year-old may not feel it is for her; the mitigation is that the scene below the arch is entirely for the child and the typography is entirely for the parent who reads the details, which is actually correct role separation for this surface; the deeper risk is that baroque depth and chiaroscuro shadow may feel dark or even frightening to the youngest viewers on the smaller themes like kittens and butterflies — these two plates must be directed with the shadow fill raised 40% and the key light softened to a window-light quality rather than a theatrical spot, preserving the depth grammar without the gothic weight; the risk is worth carrying because pink-and-glitter flatness is not safe, it is merely familiar, and a child who opens a jewel-box theatre on her phone will remember it in a

proposals.title: One Geometry, Twelve Silences
proposals.idea: Each card is a single architectural negative space — one precisely cut void that becomes a unicorn horn, a castle turret, a fin, a wing — so the enchantment lives in what is absent, not in what is added.
proposals.geometry: Fixed 390×690px portrait. A single centered die-cut silhouette occupies 55% of the vertical field; the silhouette is always bilaterally symmetric on the horizontal axis, always touching exactly one edge. The remaining field is a single-tone ground. No border. No frame. The live text zone is a 48px-high strip pinned to the bottom 12% of the card — a mechanical constant across all twelve. Grid divisions follow a 6-column, 12-row base unit of 32.5px; every element snaps to this or to half-unit (16.25px). Nothing bleeds the grid except the single silhouette.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL), Light 300, uppercase, tracking +180, size 13px — used only for the event label (UNICORN BIRTHDAY, MERMAID PARTY). Secondary: Cormorant Garamond Italic, size 22px, tracking +60 — used only for the child's name placeholder. Date and venue: DM Mono (OFL), Regular, 10px, uppercase, tracking +120. No bold weight anywhere. No color change between text and ground except the minimum contrast ratio for WCAG AA at 390px. All text is live Tela; none baked.
proposals.imageLogic: The art plate is a Magnific-generated image of a single material ground — pressed botanical paper for fairy garden, wet ink wash for mermaid, chalk-dusted velvet for ballet, spun sugar fiber for cupcake, oxidized copper foil for carousel. The silhouette void is cut from this ground: inside the void, a second Magnific-generated plate is revealed — a deep-focus environment (underwater god-rays, moonlit cloud field, backstage footlights). The two plates are composited in Tela; the void is the only window. No characters, no faces, no figures. The foreground cut-out drift layer carries one single floating object per card: a loose feather, a soap bubble, a single petal — generated, transparent PNG, physically plausible light match to the ground plate.
proposals.texture: Each ground plate is directed as a specific material with physical tooth: (1) Unicorn — spun sugar fiber, backlit, pale gold; (2) Princess Castle — cold-press watercolor paper, dry-brushed silver; (3) Mermaid — wet ink wash on Fabriano, deep teal; (4) Fairy Garden — pressed botanical paper, sage and umber; (5) Butterflies — translucent washi, rose and cream; (6) Ballet — chalk-dusted velvet, ash mauve; (7) Cupcakes — spun sugar fiber, warm white; (8) Rainbows — bleached linen, natural; (9) Kittens — soft flannel weave, warm grey; (10) Art Studio — raw gesso board, titanium white; (11) Carousel — oxidized copper foil, verdigris; (12) Pop Star — mirrored mylar, monochrome silver. Every texture is Magnific-prompted as a close-up macro photograph of the actual material — no illustration style, no painterly rendering. Texture is architecture, not decoration.
proposals.motion: Three phases, total 2.4 seconds, then idle. Phase 1 (0–0.6s): the ground plate fades in at opacity 0→1, no movement. Phase 2 (0.6–1.4s): the silhouette void appears by unmasking from center outward, eased cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) — the revealed environment inside the void brightens simultaneously, 0→1 opacity. Phase 3 (1.4–2.4s): the single floating foreground object drifts in from 8px above its rest position, settles with a 0.3s overshoot, then idles. Idle: gyroscope/pointer input drives parallax on three layers — ground (0px), void environment (±6px x/y), floating object (±14px x/y) — at 60fps, lerp factor 0.08. Scratch-and-reveal (unicorn, princess castle, mermaid, fairy garden, butterfly, pop star): the void environment is initially occluded by a second ground-texture mask at full opacity; finger/pointer drag erases the mask via a WebGL radial brush (radius 28px, feather 12px), rev
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompts: Prompt A directs 12 macro material grounds (one per theme, named above), 390×690px, physically plausible directional light from upper-left at 22°, no text, no characters, no borders — returns 12 plates. Prompt B directs 12 deep-focus environment interiors (the void-reveal content: underwater shaft of light, moonlit cloud field, backstage footlights, moss-floor forest clearing, backlit wing venation, stage resin floor reflection, glazed ceramic surface, prism-split spectrum on white wall, sleeping cat fur close-up, raw linen canvas weave, verdigris gear mechanism, mirror ball reflection arc) — returns 12 plates. Silhouette masks are procedurally generated in GLSL as SVG paths snapped to the 32.5px grid, exported as Tela-compatible vector masks. Single floating objects are Magnific-generated transparent PNGs, one per theme, with pre-multiplied alpha. WebGL scrat
proposals.humanTrace: The material ground plates are directed at macro scale so the fiber, tooth, and grain of the simulated material read as physically present — you can see the direction of the paper press, the chalk settle in velvet pile, the ink pooling at the edge of a wet wash. The silhouette mask is hand-described as a specific geometric path (not auto-traced) so its proportions carry an editorial decision, not an algorithm's average. The single floating object is selected, not generated by default — a feather rather than a sparkle, a bubble rather than a star — which is a curator's choice legible in the final frame.
proposals.risk: Children and parents conditioned to pink-and-glitter maximum may read this as cold, adult, or unfinished. The risk is worth taking because the void-as-subject strategy makes every card immediately distinct in a phone screenshot, link preview, and QR thumbnail — it reads as craft, not template — and because the scratch-and-reveal mechanic makes the absence the game: you uncover the world inside the shape, which is more legible and more memorable than uncovering decoration on top of decoration. The single floating object is the warmth valve; it keeps the card from reading as a gallery piece while preserving the structural logic.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that enchantment requires accumulation — layered light, multiple focal events, a crescendo of detail — and will want to fill the void with atmosphere, particles, and secondary characters. I disagree specifically: the void is the focal event. Adding atmosphere inside the void does not deepen it; it closes it. The scratch-and-reveal mechanic already gives the Dramatist's cre

disputes.objection: The silhouette void is a compositional idea, not a compositional system — removing all figures, faces, and characters from a child's birthday invitation in the name of architectural restraint is not formal discipline, it is a refusal to carry content; the measure is clean but nothing hangs from it, and a frame that withholds the subject is not resolving, it is evacuating. Proportion without hierarchy of meaning is ornament by subtraction, and I will not call that structural rigour simply because it is quiet. The twelve cards will read as one card in twelve materials, which is not variation — it is a single idea repeated past the point of consequence.
disputes.concession: The decision to gate the foil and shimmer strictly to the void's revealed environment rather than flooding the ground is exactly correct — restraint in the application of luster is a structural act, and the Minimalist has understood that the light source must be earned by what it illuminates.

disputes.objection: The silhouette void is a beautiful idea trapped inside its own restraint — by refusing every figure, every face, every mark of a specific hand, it produces twelve versions of the same philosophical statement rather than twelve invitations to twelve actual parties; the material grounds are directed as macro photographs of texture, which sounds rigorous, but texture with no event happening inside it is wallpaper wearing a theory; and the single floating feather, bubble, or petal is curated so carefully that the curation shows, which is the opposite of surprise — I can feel the editor's glove, not the maker's hand.
disputes.concession: The void-as-window logic — two composited plates with the silhouette cut as the only aperture — is a genuinely structural idea, not a palette choice, and I would steal that depth mechanic and put something urgent inside it.

disputes.objection: The Baroque Dramatist has written a lighting brief, not a system — 'the 2900K fresnel is placed differently for each of the twelve to match the emotional weight of the theme' is a description of twelve independent editorial decisions dressed as a rule, which means there is no propagating constraint, only twelve bespoke paintings that happen to share a proscenium silhouette; the curtain-reveal is a spectacle trigger, not a state machine, and when the input changes (different theme, different gesture speed, different screen size) the proposal has no declared behavior, only a mood; the chiaroscuro is the output, not the architecture, and I cannot build a responsive system on top of a feeling.
disputes.concession: The two-source lighting grammar — 2900K key from high-side, 6500K fill from below — is the one place where a physical constraint is named precisely enough that it could actually propagate downstream into foil highlight direction and parallax depth ordering, and that is exactly the kind of structural

disputes.objection: The material textures are named with admirable specificity — pressed botanical paper, wet ink wash on Fabriano, chalk-dusted velvet — but then the proposal instructs Magnific to generate 'a close-up macro photograph of the actual material,' which is precisely where specificity collapses into simulation of a category: there is no actual Fabriano, no actual velvet pile, no maker, no provenance, only a model's average of ten thousand unnamed textile photographs, and the proposal never acknowledges this gap or asks whose material vocabulary it is borrowing; calling it 'architecture, not decoration' does not resolve the fact that the textures are unattributed impressions of physical cultures of m
disputes.concession: The insistence that the floating foreground object be curated — a feather rather than a sparkle, a bubble rather than a star — is a genuine editorial act, and the restraint of one object per card is the kind of committed reduction that produces real visual intelligence rather than managed busyness.

disputes.objection: A silhouette void is not a reveal — it is an absence that was always there, waiting to be noticed, which is not the same as a curtain rising; the child who scratches that card away finds not a world but a peephole into another texture, and a peephole is not a stage. The scale of the emotion — a birthday, a child's name spoken aloud in gold — demands a moment that rises to meet it, and a 55% symmetric void touching one edge is a formal exercise that meets the brief the way a locked door meets a welcome. I am not arguing for excess; I am arguing that the restraint here has not decided what the work feels like, it has decided not to decide, and called that architecture.
disputes.concession: The material specificity of the ground plates is genuinely right — chalk-dusted velvet, wet ink wash on Fabriano, oxidized copper foil — these are real surfaces with real light behavior, and directing Magnific at that register of physical truth is exactly the kind of human trace that survives the ge

disputes.objection: Five depth planes, a proscenium arch, two light sources, velvet curtain physics, chiaroscuro, micro-relief die-cut edges, spun sugar, Venetian glass, worn rosin, brushed aluminium — this is not a composition, it is an inventory; each addition crowds the next until nothing can be seen because everything is insisting; the curtain reveal is dramatic precisely when the rest of the stage is quiet, but here the stage is already at full shout before the curtain moves.
disputes.concession: The decision to write the light-source position per plate into each Magnific prompt as a specific vector — not a default, not a mood, a declared angle — is structurally correct, and I would carry that discipline into my own direction.

synthesis.direction: Each of the twelve evites is a physically-simulated diorama built on three declared depth planes with a single motivated light source per theme — its angle written into every Magnific prompt and propagated into the foil-shimmer highlight direction, parallax shadow offsets, and bokeh origin, so the whole card obeys one spatial grammar. Plates are directed as painterly-but-physically-grounded generative renders (cold-press watercolour ground for soft themes, wet-glass caustic for mermaid and rainbow, matte gouache for cupcake and pop star); foreground cut-outs parallax at 0.4–1.0× tilt gain by plane; scratch-and-reveal is a depth-plane transition — not a colour change — governed by the same light source, so the scratched area reveals a lower plane with its own consistent lighting. Type is Fraunces (variable optical-size axis at 144pt italic for headline warmth) paired with DM Sans Light for date and venue; the WebGL foil shimmer lives in the frame, never bleeding onto live letterforms; two Magnific grid runs plus one GLSL shader build covers the full collection.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Baroque Dramatist's two-source lighting grammar — 2900K warm key from high-side, 6500K cool fill from below — is precise enough to propagate downstream. It survives as the declared light-source contract for the six theatrically-weighted themes (princess castle, carousel, ballet, pop star, mermaid, fairy garden); the Futurist's state-machine then enforces that those two vectors appear consistently in foil highlight angle and parallax depth ordering across every layer.
synthesis.editorCut: The Rebellious Hand removed the baroque proscenium arch and the multi-plane curtain-reveal swipe gesture. The arch is a structural frame that front-loads a genre signal (opera house, adult sophistication) before the child sees the scene — it competes with the content rather than holding it. The curtain swipe is a choreographic metaphor that works once; the Futurist's state-machine scratch-reveal works every time the card is reopened, because it is a spatial rule, not a theatrical moment. synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team split hard on this brief. The Baroque Dramatist wanted twelve miniature opera houses — proscenium arches, velvet curtain reveals, chiaroscuro at full pressure — and made a genuinely strong case that a birthday is a theatrical event that deserves a theatrical surface. The Radical Minimalist wanted the opposite: a single silhouette void per card, one floating object, nothing else. Both positions have real integrity. I chose neither.

I sided with the Futurist because the brief asks for jaw-dropping craft that works on a phone browser, loads fast, and holds up on second open. A theatrical flourish impresses once. A coherent spatial system — one motivated light source per card whose angle propagates through every layer, every shimmer, every parallax offset — impresses every time the phone tilts, because the physics are always true. That is the discipline I am recommending.

From the Baroque side I kept the two-source lighting grammar: a warm key and a cool fill, declared as specific vectors in the Magnific prompt. That is the one place the Dramatist named a physical constraint precisely enough to be buildable. The Rebellious Hand edited out the proscenium arch and the curtain-swipe reveal — not because drama is wrong, but because a frame that announces its own genre before the child sees the scene is competing with the content. The stamp-impact entrance (280ms, percussive, intentional) stays; it costs nothing and it is honest about the fact that something just arrived.

The World-Eclectic Traveler and the Classical Mind both offered real texture intelligence — the engraved-linework foil discipline and the vellum grain direction are in the Magnific prompt family. The type stack is Fraunces for headline warmth and DM Sans Light for detail legibility; both OFL, both fast. The one thing left to you is above.

quotes.line: Coherent physics is what separates a diorama from a mood board.
The drama here is in the contrast between flat ink fields and the single glinting edge — flood the foil and you lose the contrast.
